Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 92, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

.

Tafsir of Surat Wa-al-Layl (The Night)

It is Makki.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾. Qatadah said: it covers the horizon with its darkness. In another narration from him: it covers what is between the heaven and the earth with its darkness.

It was said: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾, meaning: when it becomes dark.

It is also said: it covers the day.
And His saying: ﴿By the day when it becomes manifest﴾. Its meaning: when it lights up and becomes clear. It is said: it dispels the darkness, as if he said: the darkness was dispelled by it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 92, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿And by He Who created the male and the female﴾. Ibn Mas'ud and Abu al-Darda' recited: "wa-al-dhakari wa-al-untha" (and the male and the female). This has been authenticated through their two narrations from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he recited it in this way. As for the well-known recitation: ﴿wa-ma khalaqa al-dhakara wa-al-untha﴾ (and what He created the male and the female), there are two opinions regarding it.

The first: "wa-ma khalaqa al-dhakara wa-al-untha" is like His saying: ﴿wa-al-sama'i wa-ma banaha﴾ (by the sky and He who built it), meaning: "wa-man banaha" (and He who built it).

The second opinion: "wa-ma khalaqa al-dhakara wa-al-untha" (and what He created the male and the female) is taken literally, with "ma" as a verbal noun or relative pronoun meaning "what."

Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj mentioned that "al-dhakar wa-al-untha" refers to Adam and Eve.

It has also been said that it is general, and God may swear by whatever of His creation He wills. We have already mentioned that the oath, by its implied meaning, is an invocation of the Lord, as if he said: "wa-Rabbi al-layli, wa-Rabbi al-nahari," and so on to the end.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 92, verse 4:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse.﴾ It is upon this that the oath was sworn. The meaning: indeed, your deeds are varied. It was also said: "Indeed, your efforts are diverse," meaning: among you are the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked, the grateful and the ungrateful, and similar such distinctions.

The poet said:

(The youth strives for matters that he does not attain... so the soul is one, yet the concerns are scattered.)

(And a person, as long as he lives, has an extended trace... the life does not end until the trace ends.)

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for him who gives and fears Allah﴾. Most of the commentators held that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿gives and fears Allah﴾ means: he spends his wealth in charity and is mindful of Allah the Exalted.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And affirms the best reward﴾ — that is, [affirms] the creation by God Exalted; this was said by ʿIkrima, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, and it is the most well-known of the opinions.

The second opinion: "And affirms the best reward," that is, [affirms] Paradise; this was said by Mujahid.

It was also said: [it means] the reward. Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami and ʿAta said: "And affirms the best reward" means: [affirms] "There is no god but God."

And His words: ﴿So We will ease him toward ease﴾ — i.e., toward the state of ease. The meaning: the path of acts of obedience (al-ta'at) and righteous deeds becomes easy for him. Al-Azhari said: He makes easy for him that which is made easy only for the Muslims.

Almost the whole passage is a quotation from the Qur'an and some commentary. Translating faithfully:

God Most High says: ﴿But as for him who is niggardly and considers himself self-sufficient﴾. It is said: the verse was revealed concerning Umayya ibn Khalaf, and it is also said: concerning Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.

And His words ﴿is niggardly﴾ mean: he withheld his wealth; and ﴿considers himself self-sufficient﴾ means: he was independent of the reward of his Lord.
And His saying: ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾ — it is what we have explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 92, verse 10:

And His saying: ﴿So We will ease him toward the difficult path.﴾ That is: He makes the path of evil easy for him. Abu Salih narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He prevents him from faith in Allah and His Messenger.

Al-Farra' said: If someone asks, "How is His saying ﴿So We will ease him toward the difficult path﴾ correct, and how can ease be applied to hardship?" He answers: This is like His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾. He placed "tidings" in the position of the threat of the Fire, even though it was not tidings in reality. Likewise, "easing" is placed in this position, even though it is in reality making difficult.

It has been mentioned by 'Ata' al-Khurasani that the verse was revealed concerning a man of the Ansar who had a garden, and he had a palm tree whose branches hung over the house of his neighbour, and the neighbour would eat from what fell from its fruit. The Ansari prevented him, so that poor man complained of this to the Messenger of Allah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to the Ansari: "Sell me this palm tree for a palm tree of yours in Paradise." He refused to sell. Abu al-Dahdah bought it from him for a garden of his, and gave it to that poor man. So Allah, exalted is He, revealed these verses concerning both of them.

The more correct view is that the verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), because the surah is Meccan according to the consensus, so it is not sound that the verse was revealed concerning any of the Ansar.

There is a sound report concerning these two verses, which is what Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir narrated from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "We were at a funeral in al-Baqi', and the Prophet came and sat, and we sat with him. He had a stick with which he was scratching the ground. He raised his head to the sky and said: 'There is no soul created but that its place of entry has been written.' The people said: 'O Messenger of Allah, should we not rely on our writing? Whoever is among the people of happiness will act for happiness, and whoever is among the people of misery will act for misery.' He said: 'No, act, for each is made easy. As for the one who is of the people of happiness, he is made easy for the deeds of happiness, and as for the one who is of the people of misery, he is made easy for the deeds of misery.' Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best reward, We will ease him toward ease. But as for he who is stingy and considers himself free of need, and denies the best reward, We will ease him toward the difficult path.﴾"

He said, may Allah be pleased with him: Abu 'Ali al-Shafi'i informed us of this in Mecca; Abu al-Hasan ibn Faras informed us; al-Dibili informed us; Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi informed us; Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna informed us, from Mansur, the hadith.

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls (tardā)﴾. Its meaning: when he perishes. It is said: tarrā (tardā) means he fell into the Fire, and this is the more correct view, because tardī in the language means falling. It is said: he fell (tarrā) from such-and-such a place, meaning he dropped.

And His words, ﴿Indeed, to Us belongs guidance﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: "Upon Us is the clarification of what is lawful and what is unlawful, and of obedience and disobedience."

It is also said: whoever takes the path of guidance, then guiding him is upon Us, like His words ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾, meaning: the clarification of the way for whoever intends it.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first [life]﴾. That is, the dominion of the Hereafter and of the first [life]. It has also been said: the reward of the Hereafter and of the first [life].

The commentary on surah 92, verse 14:

And His saying: ﴿I have warned you of a Fire that blazes⟩ (fa-andhartukum nāran talaẓẓā). Its meaning: tatalaẓẓā (it blazes), and its sense: tatawahhaj (it flares up and glows intensely).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 92, verses 15–16:

And His saying: ﴿None will enter it except the most wretched, who denied and turned away﴾, meaning: who denied Allah and turned away from obedience to Him.

In the verse there is an objection to the Murji'a and the Khawarij. For Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿None will enter it except the most wretched﴾, meaning: none will endure its heat and none will enter it except the most wretched, who denied and turned away. This indicates that a believer, even if he commits major sins, does not enter the Fire. This is the position against the Murji'a. As for the Khawarij, they said: "You have agreed with us that the companion of major sins enters the Fire, so this indicates that he becomes a disbeliever by committing a major sin, and he joins those who denied and turned away, since Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿None will enter it except the most wretched who denied and turned away﴾."

The answer comes in several aspects. The first: its meaning is: none will enter it except the most wretched who denied and turned away. The "most wretched" are the people of major sins, and "those who denied and turned away" are the disbelievers.

The Arabs say: "I ate bread, meat, dates" (khubzan lahman tamran), meaning: "and meat and dates," and they omitted the conjunction (waw). Likewise here. Abu Zayd al-Ansari recited:

(Kayfa asbahta, kayfa amsayta, fama ... yuthbitu al-wudd fi fu'ad al-karim)

meaning: "And how did you spend the evening?"

The second aspect: the Fire has levels (darakat), and what is meant by the verse is one specific level, which only disbelievers enter. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire﴾. The verse indicates that it is specific to the hypocrites. This is a well-known answer.

The third aspect: the meaning is: none will enter it to remain in it forever (la yusallaha, la yadkhuluha khalidan fiha) except the most wretched who denied and turned away. The companion of a major sin, even if he enters it, will not remain in it forever.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 92, verses 17–18:

And His saying: ﴿And the most righteous will be kept away from it, the one who gives his wealth to purify himself﴾. That is: he gives his wealth so that he becomes pure and clean. It is reported concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, according to the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun). It is said that the first verse was revealed concerning Umayya ibn Khalaf. As for his giving of wealth, it is that he freed seven persons who were being tortured for the sake of Allah, among them Bilal al-Khayr, Amir ibn Fuhayra, al-Nahdiyya, Zunayra, and others.

It is also narrated that when he bought Zunayra and freed her, she having embraced Islam, she soon went blind. The polytheists said: "Al-Lat and al-Uzza have blinded her." She said: "I deny al-Lat and al-Uzza," so Allah restored her sight to her.

It is well known that the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by Bilal while he was being tortured on the burning sands of Makkah, and he was saying: "One, One." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Ahad (the One) will deliver you." Then he came to Abu Bakr and said: "I saw Bilal being tortured for the sake of Allah." So Abu Bakr went to his house, took a ratl of gold, came to Umayya ibn Khalaf, bought him from him and freed him. The Quraysh said: "He freed him only because he has a debt of favour owed to him by him."

The Quraysh said: "He freed him only because he has a debt of favour owed to him by him."

Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And no one has any favor with him that is repaid, except seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High.﴾ That is: except seeking the pleasure of his Lord, the Exalted.

Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And no one has any favor with him that is repaid, except seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High.﴾ That is: except seeking the pleasure of his Lord, the Exalted.

And His words: ﴿And surely He will give you so much that you will be well-pleased﴾ — meaning: He will be pleased with His reward for him in the Hereafter; the sense is that Allah will give him until he is pleased.

Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir that Jibril (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet and said: "Tell Abu Bakr that Allah the Exalted says: 'I am pleased with you; are you pleased with Me?'" So this was mentioned to Abu Bakr, [and he wept] and fell prostrate, and said: "I am pleased with my Lord, I am pleased with my Lord."

And it was narrated from Ali that the Prophet said: "May Allah have mercy on Abu Bakr: he gave me his daughter in marriage, carried me to the abode of the Hijrah, and bought Bilal and freed him."
